messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High-rate streaming errors observed for customer 'Orchid Financial' (vpc-tenant-547) hitting app-gateway. Error class: downstream websocket timeouts (502/504). Paging on-call.
sre_jamie: saw the bot. I'm taking first-touch. oncall-ml, can you join? looks like spikes at 02:23 UTC.
oncall-ml: joining now. any customer-reported behavior? Orchid oncall, are your users seeing disconnects or degraded responses?

orchid_oncall: yes, customers report intermittent streaming drops and partial transcripts; some sessions fall back to reconnect loop. Started ~02:22 UTC, affecting ~12% of sessions. We're on standby on our side.

eng-runtime-chi: digging into gateway logs now — pattern: client WS opens, then backend inference pool returns 504 after 20s. I see short bursts of retry storms from same tenant IP CIDR. Possibly request pacing + backend queue pressure.

solutions_alia: Orchid uses our dedicated GPU pool 'dedicated-ord-3' with tenant isolation. Could this be overflow to shared fallback? any routing changes recently?

eng-runtime-chi: routing shows requests were briefly routed to fallback variant (quantized-1) at 02:21 due to autoscaler signal. Fallbacks are healthy but streaming path didn't gracefully degrade — ws proxy returned 502 when backend closed connection during token stream.

pm_liam: customer impact: 12% sessions, realtime transcription degraded; business-critical for Orchid — request immediate mitigation and a coordinated bridge with customer. paging alert: escalation to ENG-FEATURES and SRE.

incident-bot: conference bridge created: https://meet.redwood/bridges/3456789999

sre_jamie: mitigation idea 1: throttle per-tenant concurrency at proxy (soft cap 8) to stop retry storm. mitigation idea 2: enable streaming->polling fallback for existing sessions so clients can continue via short-polling. Which is faster to ship?

oncall-ml: throttle at proxy is config flip. Polling fallback requires client-side change but we can server-side offer chunked polling endpoint. I can flip throttle immediately and add short-term increase in backend request timeout from 20s -> 45s to reduce mid-stream terminations.

eng-runtime-chi: changing backend timeout now. Command: ``kubectl -n runtime exec configmap/proxy-config -- patch -p '{"data":{"backend_timeout":"45s","per_tenant_concurrency":"8"}}'`` applying.

incident-bot: deploy bot: configmap patched by eng-runtime-chi @3456789945 — rollout started.

orchid_oncall: appreciate quick response. can you also whitelist our active IPs? we saw retries from our old proxy IPs as well.

solutions_alia: confirmed: Orchid has two CIDRs; we'll add both to the allowed upstream list to avoid misrouting. doing that now.

eng-runtime-chi: backend timeout applied. proxy reports per-tenant token buckets engaged. early telemetry shows streaming error rate drop from 12% -> 4% in first 60s.

oncall-ml: also turning on streaming->polling fallback for sessions that hit ws handshake failures. patching gateway route to accept header `x-rw-fallback: polling` and queue requests into short-poll broker. applying route change with: ```curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood/config/routes/streaming -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"fallback_enabled":true}'``` — done @3456790088

eng-runtime-chi: prod metrics: 1-minute window shows tail latency for streaming down from 28s->11s; error count still trending down. Orchids' oncall, any change on your end?

orchid_oncall: sessions that previously dropped are reconnecting and receiving polling chunks. A handful still see reconnect thrash but it's much better. We're good to keep this as active mitigation for next 30m.

pm_liam: note for customer communications: send an interim update acknowledging mitigation and that we are investigating root cause (autoscaler mis-signal + retry amplification). Solutions, draft a short note.

solutions_alia: drafting: "We're seeing transient gateway scaling signals that briefly routed traffic to a fallback model and caused websocket session resets under retry storms. We've implemented per-tenant throttling, extended backend timeouts, and enabled streaming->polling fallback. Impact reduced; we're continuing to monitor and will follow up with RCA." Sending to Orchid legal/reg team via DM.

eng-runtime-chi: follow-up runbook items: 1) audit autoscaler thresholds for dedicated pools, 2) add guardrail to prevent fallback for active streaming sessions, 3) add per-tenant emergent backpressure metric and alert. I'll open tasks.

oncall-ml: opening incident task board: https://boards.redwood/incident/3456789999/tasks

incident-bot: on-call Handoff: SRE shift ends in 25m; @sre_jamie please hand to night-shift @oncall-ml after 30m; include mitigation steps and flags to watch (streaming_error_rate > 2% for 5m, per-tenant concurrency saturating >80%).

sre_jamie: will do. leaving notes in thread and handoff doc. current status: mitigation in place, error rate dropping. next action: monitor for 1 hour, then start RCA.

orchid_oncall: thanks team. we'll stay on the bridge for next 20m and validate at our side. appreciate the rapid mitigation. we'll need a post-incident timeline for our compliance team.

pm_liam: assign postmortem owners: eng-runtime-chi (root cause), solutions_alia (customer comms), oncall-ml (mitigation verification). Target postmortem initial draft in 48h.

incident-bot: incident severity downgraded to S2 @3456790300 — customer impact reduced, active mitigations in place.

eng-runtime-chi: quick note: initial hypothesis = autoscaler signalled low capacity due to transient metric smear during GC spike in dedicated pool; fallback route didn't handle streaming gracefully. We'll surface kernel traces and pod logs in RCA.

oncall-ml: monitoring shows sustained improvement. I'll stay on watch and escalate if error rate rises above 2%.

orchid_oncall: we've captured sample session IDs and will share logs via secure dropbox link: https://files.orchid/stream-samples/3456789999 — sending now.

solutions_alia: got the samples. thanks. I'll include them in RCA artifacts.

sre_jamie: handing off to @oncall-ml now. oncall-ml, please confirm you have runbook and can continue watch.

oncall-ml: confirmed. I have runbook, alerts, and the bridge. closing active paging but keeping incident thread open for updates.


incident-bot: incident thread locked for summary generation in 24h.
